ETH Zurich (German: Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule Zürich; English: Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich) is a public university in Zurich, Switzerland. Founded by the Swiss federal government in 1854, the university primarily teaches and conducts research in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). ETH Zurich is widely regarded as one of the world's leading universities, particularly in the sciences, and consistently ranks among the top universities worldwide.[7][8][9][10]
Like its sister institution École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), ETH Zurich is part of the Swiss Federal Institutes of Technology Domain, a consortium of universities and research institutes under the Swiss Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research.[11] As of 2025, ETH Zurich enrolled 26,942 students, of whom 4,266 were pursuing doctoral degrees.[5]

ETH Zurich was founded on 7 February 1854 by the Swiss Confederation and began giving its first lectures on 16 October 1855 as a polytechnic institute (eidgenössische polytechnische Schule) at various sites throughout the city of Zurich.[1]

From 1905 to 1908, under the presidency of Jérôme Franel, ETH Zurich restructured its course programs to those of a university and was granted the right to award doctorates. The first doctorates were awarded in 1909. In 1911, the institution received its current name, Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule. Another reorganization in 1924 structured the university into 12 departments. Today, it has 16 departments.
ETH Zurich, along with EPFL and four associated research institutes, forms the "ETH Domain" to collaborate on scientific projects.[16]

ETH Zurich (Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule Zürich) is a public university in Zurich, Switzerland, with a focus on science, technology, engineering and mathematics. It is a federal institution and belongs to the ETH Domain, which also includes EPFL and four research institutes. Its teaching and research are organized into 16 departments, with degree programmes extending from bachelor’s and master’s study to doctorates. German and English are used in teaching, with English used at master’s level and above and in some bachelor’s courses.

The Swiss Confederation founded the institution on 7 February 1854, and its first lectures began on 16 October 1855 under the name eidgenössische polytechnische Schule. The German account and Wikidata use 1855 as its founding or inception year. Its first doctorates were awarded in 1909, and it adopted the name Eidgenössische Technische Hochschule in 1911. The university has campuses at Zentrum and Hönggerberg in Zurich, and established a satellite campus in Basel in 2007 for biosystems science and engineering. A teaching and research centre in Heilbronn began operating in early 2025, focusing on responsible digital transformation. In 2025, ETH Zurich reported 26,942 students, including 4,266 doctoral students, and a budget of CHF 2.051 billion.
